title: Charcoal Filter Doesn’t Adequately Seal Off Holes in Stainless Steel Lid
text:
Charcoal Filter Doesn’t Adequately Seal Off Holes in Stainless Steel Lid. This UTOPIA KITCHEN STAINLESS STEEL COMPOST BIN (for Kitchen Countertop;1.3 Gallon with Lid, Charcoal Filter, 1 Spare Charcoal Filter) is ideally sized for an indoor compost bin, and it has a tight-fitting lid. However, the lid has large holes in it, and the charcoal filter inside the lid is see-through thin.

Thus the bin is a poor choice for my household, because we are constantly battling the ants that have colonized large portions of the Northern California coast. The thin filter may contain odors--or may not--but it doesn’t present an adequate barrier to ants that are attracted by food scrap odors.

When the bin is lined with a compostable bag, the lid fits too snugly, and is hard to remove. The charcoal filter is somewhat hard to pull out and replace, despite the seller's instructions to keep it free of food residue and to sun dry it weekly to avoid microbial growth.

I like the pail handle, and the bin size, and the all-stainless-steel construction. However, this bin won’t work for me, because I want the bin to hold food scraps indoors overnight for later transfer to a big outdoor compost cart.
